Care standards for gate calls
Staff will learn how the desk handles it
Companion Animal Travel Desk Care Standards

This section sets out how the Companion Animal Travel Desk at Aurelia Skyways should support travelers and protect animals with calm, clear handling. The goal is to keep the process kind, orderly, and easy to follow for both guests and staff.

When a traveler contacts the desk, the tone should stay warm and professional, even if the situation feels rushed. Staff should listen carefully, give simple guidance, and avoid jargon whenever possible. If a traveler arrives with a pet such as Ollie, the agent should confirm the file is complete, answer basic concerns, and pass the case along without delay when a specialist review is needed. <<FACT F086>> The desk should never guess at missing details or promise an exception that has not been approved.

<<FACT F092>> Staff should treat that step as fixed and should not try to stretch it or soften it with casual wording. If a traveler asks for help after that point, the agent should explain the limits politely and record the contact so the next team member can see what happened.

The desk should also watch for animal comfort and travel readiness. Crates, labels, and travel notes should be reviewed with care, and any sign of distress should be reported at once to the cabin team. The cabin team monitors animals during flight, so the desk must make sure the handoff is clean and the notes are easy to read. If a traveler like Anika Silva or Ravi Brown shares a concern, staff should stay patient, avoid blame, and focus on the next safe step.

If the situation is unclear, the agent should pause and escalate instead of improvising. This is not meant to make the work cold; it is meant to keep animals safe and reduce confusion for everyone involved. For questions about exceptions or escalations, contact the senior coordinator through the normal internal channel.
